Design and manage the execution of credible and feasible evaluations that address identified purposes and questions. Formative and summative evaluation: Identify quality improvement opportunities and develop recommendations to strengthen program services and organizational operations. Negotiate and manage timelines and document evaluation processes and products Develop and implement processes for data collection and analysis: Develop qualitative and quantitative data collection tools for evaluation, including, but not limited to, interview guides, focus group guides, surveys, etc. Ensure data quality and participate in data integrity review Conduct review of literature to justify appropriate methods to answer evaluation questions and identify assumptions that underlie methodologies and program logic. The candidate must be legally authorized to work in the U.S.  Application Deadline: ​Until filled; use the online form provided at karunacenter.org/jobs to apply. Anticipated Job Start Date: ​Mid to late October 2026 Salary range: $75,000 - $85,000 for full-time, or $60,000 - $66,000 if hired at 32 hours per week, with the salary based on the level of experience and expertise About Karuna Center for Peacebuilding Karuna Center empowers communities to build peace by working across divides to transform conflict and strengthen resilience to violence. Through collaborative projects co-led with local partner organizations, we support people directly impacted by conflict to build trust across divides, strengthen social cohesion, and create ongoing systems for de-escalating potential violence. Our approach engages whole communities, including those whose voices are often left out of peacebuilding, and includes advocacy with government and civil society for community-based peacebuilding. Karuna Center has worked in more than 35 conflict-affected countries since 1994, with current programs focused primarily in West Africa and the United States. Learn more about Karuna Center at www.karunacenter.org . The Opportunity  Karuna Center for Peacebuilding is pleased to announce an open position for a Program Finance Manager.  This specialized role is focused on the financial management of Karuna’s international projects, with special attention to improving systems, policies, and processes; on regulatory compliance; and on capacity-building for subrecipients’ finance team. Managing grants funded by the U.S. Department of State, the successful candidate will specialize in translating federal compliance standards (2 CFR 200) into practical, accessible templates and workflows that improve efficiency on our end and that work well for our grassroots international partners. The role also involves creating and managing budgets for proposals and funded programs and supporting work on the annual audit. This is a new, hands-on position that will be an integral part of our small, highly collaborative virtual office team. Pending grant funding, this role will either be an 80%  (32 hours per week) position or a full-time position.  The Program Finance Manager works directly with Karuna’s program team and with the finance and program staff of our international subrecipients, who are valued local peacebuilding partner organizations of varying sizes and financial competencies. Currently, work in this role focuses on four subrecipients in Nigeria carrying out community-based peacebuilding to prevent violence. The ideal candidate excels both at working with numbers and working with people and will have experience working on subrecipient financial management for peacebuilding, development, or humanitarian organizations, as well as proven competency in cross-cultural communication. The Program Finance Manager reports directly to the Executive Director, engages with the bookkeeping firm, and collaborates with the Program Managers and the part-time Program Finance Coordinator. This is hands-on work that includes monthly review of payment requests, oversight of program staff’s review of receipts and expense reports, quarterly close out of subrecipient budget vs. actuals documents, occasional budget amendments, and financial close-out of projects when grant period ends Ensure program financial management processes are informed by a working understanding of program implementation and progress Train subrecipient finance teams, including occasional international travel for in-person capacity-building, and engage in ongoing mentoring Stay updated on changes in 2 CFR 200 to ensure ongoing regulatory compliance, and use that knowledge to update and/or draft organizational and program policies related to the financial management of projects and of subrecipients Assist with program proposals, working closely with the technical team and host country partners to develop project budgets and support the writing of the budget narrative  Support the program team and bookkeeping firm in providing documents for the annual audit and engage with auditors around program finance policies and procedures Support for Operations and Finance Time permitting, support discrete tasks related to organizational operations and finance  Qualifications and Skills  5+ years relevant experience in the financial management of U.S. government grants, especially DOS and/or USAID grants. Experience working with partners in West Africa is a plus  3+ years experience managing subrecipient budgets in international currencies Demonstrated competency in optimizing systems for the financial management of international subrecipients, based on a deep knowledge of 2 CFR 200 Ability to apply a coaching mentality for engagement with subrecipients. Experience training and mentoring international subrecipients in the financial management of projects a plus Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to engage effectively with a wide range of people across cultures, with fluency in English required  Excellent numeracy skills, with strong attention to detail required High proficiency in Excel and Google Sheets. Working knowledge of QuickBooks a plus Ability to be well-organized, manage multiple tasks simultaneously, and meet deadlines   Resourcefulness in problem-solving, initiative to learn new skills, and passion for continuous improvement in processes Positive attitude, team player, and commitment to Karuna Center’s mission  Flexibility and adaptability to support the success of Karuna’s programs Working Conditions:  Work performed at home with considerable time using a computer Will include occasional international travel to Abuja, Nigeria and other international contexts where Karuna works Hours generally conform to a standard work day in Eastern Standard or Daylight Time, with some flexibility needed to collaborate effectively with partners across world time zones, and especially those working in West Africa. There is room for limited flexibility in one’s work schedule when needed.  Collaborative, informal office culture, on a small, remote team that engages with multiple consultants and international partners Benefits:  Health insurance: After a 3-month probationary period, Karuna Center covers the cost of health insurance premiums, up to $1040 per month, for either an individual or family health insurance policy Paid holidays*: 12 paid holidays per year Paid vacation: 15 days (3 weeks) paid vacation the first year, increasing to 21 days (4 weeks plus 1 day) after that Paid sick days*: Up to 10 paid sick days per year, including up to 3 days for care for an immediate family member. Family and Medical and Other Leave Benefits: Karuna Center provides Family Medical Leave and other leave benefits, consistent with the laws of the State in which its employees work remotely. *In the event an employee works remotely in a state that requires a higher benefit, the higher benefit will apply. review_candidates.title: Platform Architect
review_candidates.description: Welcome to KTO Group, where innovation drives excitement in iGaming. Founded in 2018 by Andreas Bardun, we’re transforming online gaming with a focus on transparency and player satisfaction. At KTO.com , we blend the thrill of sports betting with online casino entertainment, tailored to local markets and powered by our proprietary platform for a seamless, personalized experience. KTO is a rising leader in LATAM, proudly ranked among Brazil’s top 10 iGaming brands. Join us as we set new standards in trust, innovation, and the future of iGaming. We are investing in the next generation of our platform: a new real-time, event-driven foundation that will change how KTO understands and serves its players. This role is its first dedicated hire — the Platform Architect who lays the foundation everything else will be built on. Most of what happens on a sportsbook and casino is understood after the fact. We want to change that. We are building an event-driven platform that captures what is happening across our products as it happens, and a decision layer on top of it that lets KTO respond to players in real time. This is not a maintenance role and it is not a seat on an existing team. You are engineer #1 on a foundation-level project with executive sponsorship. You work in a tight loop with the project lead and you own the technical architecture end to end. You stay hands-on all the way to production. You're expected to move fast, including by pairing heavily with AI tools for day-to-day engineering work — this isn't a nice-to-have here, it's how the early build actually happens with a team this size. Key Responsibilities Define the event contracts that our backend and frontend teams must produce to, and every downstream consumer will depend on. Build the ingestion edge that enforces them and adapts existing events into line. Own the stream-processing and low-latency state layer that turns raw events into real-time signals. Design and ship the rules/decisioning layer that turns those signals into actions — fast, explainable and safe. Define delivery guarantees, versioning, replay strategy, and privacy-by-design for the event platform, given Brazil's regulatory environment. Learn the business deeply enough to be able to scope the first production use case, then take it end to end — from idea, through architecture, to a live system — documenting the pattern other engineers will follow after. Translate business requirements from the project lead into technical design, present architecture trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders, and manage competing priorities as they come up. Set the initial technical standards (code, review, on-call, incident process) this effort runs on. Build measurement from day one: every decision logged with the facts it used, a permanent hold-back group, and the ability to replay any rule against history. The platform must be able to prove its own value, not just act. Main Requirements Fluent English, with strong written and verbal communication — you'll work directly with senior leadership. Real-time systems architecture knowledge — non-negotiable. Production experience building and operating event-driven systems (Kafka or similar), including debugging and fixing real incidents. Experience owning schema and data contracts as long-lived interfaces other teams depend on. Hands-on experience with stream processing and low-latency state: out-of-order events, exactly-once delivery, cancellable timers. Experience building or integrating rules, decisioning, or real-time personalisation systems. Track record of making architecture decisions under uncertainty. Curiosity and a self-starter mindset. Nice to have Experience in iGaming, payments, fintech, or another regulated, high-volume consumer domain. Experience being engineer #1 on a platform effort — knowing what to build now versus later. Familiarity with frontend event instrumentation and client-side telemetry. At KTO, diversity isn't just a buzzword – it's our strength.
